result.question:
Find concrete, downloadable public datasets and resources to serve as sample/test data for building "Grader", a local-first AI grading app for higher-ed instructors. For EVERY dataset found, report: exact name, direct download/access URL, license/terms (commercial vs research-only vs CC), size/item count, whether it includes HUMAN SCORES/GRADES (essential), whether it includes RUBRICS, format, and any access barriers (Kaggle account, signed data-use agreement, request form). Needed:

(1) GRADED-WRITING / AUTOMATED-ESSAY-SCORING datasets with human scores AND ideally rubrics: ASAP-AES (Hewlett/Kaggle), ASAP-SAS (short answer scoring), Feedback Prize (Kaggle: Evaluating Student Writing / English Language Learning / Predicting Effective Arguments), ELLIPSE corpus, PERSUADE 2.0 corpus, TOEFL11/ETS corpora, ICLE, IELTS/writing-score datasets on HuggingFace, CommonLit Readability, Kaggle "Learning Agency Lab" datasets, AES benchmarks used in 2024-2026 LLM-grading papers. Include HuggingFace Hub dataset IDs where they exist.

(2) SHORT-ANSWER / STEM / PROBLEM-SET grading datasets: ASAP-SAS, SciEntsBank / Beetle (SemEval-2013 Task 7 student response analysis), Mohler & Mihalcea short answer grading dataset, EdNet, NAEP/MCAS released items with scoring guides, physics/math graded-response corpora, CS code-grading datasets (e.g., autograded student code with human scores), Dataset(s) used in "K-12 GenAI assessment graders" / EduAdapt / rubric-conditioned-grading papers (arXiv 2510.17389, 2606.12422).

(3) RUBRIC corpora: public university rubric libraries (AAC&U VALUE rubrics — license/usage terms), Canvas Commons rubrics, published rubric datasets, and any datasets pairing rubric + student work + score.

(4) HANDWRITTEN student work / handwriting OCR datasets: IAM Handwriting Database (access terms), CVL, RIMES, Kaggle handwritten math (CROHME, Aida/im2latex, "handwritten mathematical expressions"), NIST, handwritten exam/answer-sheet datasets, the dataset from arXiv 2606.11477 (handwritten exam answer recognition) — is it public?, HuggingFace handwriting datasets, and any datasets of scanned/photographed graded student exams.

(5) DOCUMENT-PARSING test corpora: DocLayNet, OmniDocBench, PubLayNet, academic PDFs with known structure — for validating the Docling pipeline.

(6) CITATION / REFERENCE-VERIFICATION fixtures: datasets of real vs fabricated/hallucinated citations (LLM-hallucinated reference datasets from 2023-2026 papers), retracted-paper lists, papers with known-bad bibliographies, Crossref/OpenAlex test DOIs, and any corpus of student papers WITH bibliographies.

(7) CANVAS LMS TEST ENVIRONMENT: how an individual developer gets a free Canvas instance to test grade write-back — Canvas Free-for-Teacher account (canvas.instructure.com free tier: capabilities/limits), Instructure's test/beta environments, running Canvas LMS open-source locally via Docker, Canvas API sandbox options. Include signup URLs and what API scopes/tokens are available.

For each of the 7 categories, end with a RECOMMENDATION: which 1-2 resources to actually use, and note explicitly if a category has NO good public option.
result.summary: Three of the seven requested categories now have concrete, verified, downloadable answers: graded-writing/AES, short-answer/STEM grading, and rubric corpora. The strongest single find is ASAP 2.0 (~24,278 source-based argumentative essays, human holistic 1-6 scores, CC BY 4.0 — the only major graded-writing corpus that is commercially usable — with a rubric PDF that downloads anonymously); it is best paired with PERSUADE 2.0 and ELLIPSE, both of which ship actual scoring rubrics alongside student work and human scores but are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial). For short-answer/STEM grading, ASAG2024 (HuggingFace: Meyerger/ASAG2024) already packages SciEntsBank, Beetle II, Mohler and four others into one human-graded, normalized corpus, and the 2026 S-GRADES benchmark consolidates 14 AES+ASAG datasets — though S-GRADES withholds test-split labels and its redistribution is research-scoped. For rubrics, AAC&U's 16 VALUE rubrics are free and downloadable but explicitly name "assessment software or digital products" as a commercial use requiring prior written permission from AAC&U — a direct constraint on shipping them as built-in templates in Grader. Critically, categories 4 (handwriting/scanned exams), 5 (document-parsing corpora), 6 (citation/hallucinated-reference fixtures), and 7 (Canvas LMS test environment) produced ZERO claims that survived adversarial verification in this pass — they are unanswered, not answered-negatively, and need a dedicated second research pass.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 1 TOP PICK — ASAP 2.0 is the best AES dataset for Grader: ~24,278 human-scored argumentative essays under CC BY 4.0 (commercially usable), with a publicly downloadable holistic scoring rubric.
findings.evidence:
NAME: ASAP 2.0 (Automated Student Assessment Prize 2.0), The Learning Agency Lab + Vanderbilt (Crossley et al.).
SIZE: 24,278 essays in the full corpus release; the Kaggle competition train.csv is 17,307 labeled essays (columns: essay_id, full_text, score). Kaggle dataset mirror is ~23 MB, updated 2025-12-05.
HUMAN SCORES: YES — holistic 1-6, human-rated. The ~13k PERSUADE-derived essays were scored by 20 expert human raters, double-blind with 100% adjudication (pre-adjudication weighted kappa .745). Competition metric is QWK, which is only meaningful against human raters.
RUBRIC: YES — the official 'Holistic Essay Scoring' rubric PDF (4 pages, two rubrics: source-based and independent writing, full SCORE OF 6 -> SCORE OF 1 descriptors) was verified to download anonymously over plain HTTPS with NO Kaggle login (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 83,477 bytes). GitHub repo also carries asap_scoring_rubric.docx.
LICENSE: CC BY 4.0 — commercial reuse permitted with attribution. This is the ONLY major graded-writing corpus in this report that is commercially usable without asking permission.
FORMAT: CSV (essay text + score + prompt/source text + demographics); rubric as PDF/DOCX.
ACCESS BARRIERS: The Kaggle *dataset* route (lburleigh/asap-2-0) needs only a free Kaggle account — and an unauthenticated API download actually returned HTTP 200. The Kaggle *competition* /data route additionally requires signing in and accepting competition rules (unauthenticated API probes return HTTP 401). Use the dataset mirror or the GitHub repo, not the competition page. Note the test split in the GitHub release is a password-protected archive (password: asap2_test).
CAVEATS: essays are grades 6-10 (K-12), NOT higher-ed; all are source-based/argumentative; scores are holistic only, not per-trait analytic sub-scores; ~12,871 of the 24,278 essays are re-used from PERSUADE 2.0, so ASAP 2.0 and PERSUADE 2.0 OVERLAP and must not be double-counted; the 'largest open-access writing dataset' superlative is the publisher's own marketing line, not an independently benchmarked fact; the Learning Agency Lab page states the org 'is no longer active,' so long-term hosting of the landing page is uncertain (the Kaggle mirror is live and current).
RECOMMENDATION (Category 1): Use ASAP 2.0 as the primary AES fixture set (CC BY = safe to bundle). Add ELLIPSE or PERSUADE 2.0 as a second, rubric-rich set for internal dev/eval only.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 1 SECOND PICK — PERSUADE 2.0 (25,996 essays, grades 6-12) is the richest rubric+work+score triple, shipping three real scoring rubric PDFs, but is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).
findings.evidence:
NAME: PERSUADE 2.0 (Crossley, Baffour, Tian, Franklin, Benner, Boser — Assessing Writing, doi 10.1016/j.asw.2024.100865).
SIZE: 25,996 argumentative essays, grades 6-12 U.S. students, 15 prompts, split into independent and source-based writing tasks.
HUMAN SCORES: YES, two kinds — (a) holistic essay scores 1-6 from trained human raters on a modified SAT holistic rubric; (b) per-element proficiency/effectiveness labels (Ineffective / Adequate / Effective) for each argumentative discourse element (Lead, Position, Claim, Counterclaim, Rebuttal, Evidence, Concluding Statement). This is the Feedback Prize lineage.
RUBRICS: YES — three rubric PDFs verified present in the repo tree by GitHub API and opened: argumentation_effectiveness_rubric.pdf (83,254 B, 4 pages, per-element Effective/Adequate/Ineffective descriptors with worked examples), sat_rubric_only_indy.pdf (11,505 B, 1-page holistic 1-6 rating form), sat_rubric_only_source_based.pdf (13,591 B).
LICENSE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — NonCommercial. Fine for internal dev/testing/benchmarking; a commercial Grader cannot bundle it as shipped sample data or train on it without separate permission from the authors.
FORMAT: rubrics as PDF in the git repo; the essay/score CSVs are TOO LARGE for GitHub and are hosted on Google Drive (persuade_2.0_human_scores_demo_id_github.csv); test set is a password-protected zip (password: persuade_test). Kaggle mirror: nbroad/persaude-corpus-2. Zenodo record: 8221504.
ACCESS BARRIERS: none hard — Google Drive link + published zip password; Kaggle mirror needs a free account.
CAVEATS: K-12 (grades 6-12), not higher-ed. Overlaps ASAP 2.0 by ~12,871 essays. NOTE ON LICENSE VERIFICATION: a claim asserting the NC license *plus* a redistribution prohibition was REFUTED 0-3 — the license fact (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) is confirmed by the repo, but the refuted claim over-reached: ShareAlike DOES permit redistribution under the same license; the real blocker is commercial use, not redistribution.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 1 THIRD PICK — ELLIPSE is the only corpus found that pairs a downloadable rubric file with ANALYTIC (multi-trait) human sub-scores: ~6,500 ELL essays with a holistic score plus six trait scores.
findings.evidence:
NAME: ELLIPSE (English Language Learner Insight, Proficiency and Skills Evaluation) Corpus — Crossley et al. 2023, Int'l Journal of Learner Corpus Research 9(2):248-269. Basis of the Kaggle 'Feedback Prize - English Language Learning' competition.
SIZE: ~6,500 ELL writing samples, grades 8-12.
HUMAN SCORES: YES — each essay scored by TWO trained human raters. One holistic 'Overall' score plus SIX analytic sub-scores: Cohesion, Syntax, Vocabulary, Phraseology, Grammar, Conventions. This is the only dataset here giving per-trait analytic human scores, which is the closest match to how a rubric-driven grader actually behaves.
RUBRIC: YES — ELL_Rubrics.docx (17,420 B) was downloaded and its XML extracted: it is a real 'English Proficiency Scoring Rubric for English Language Learners' with a HOLISTIC column and analytic columns matching the six traits, each with full prose level descriptors (e.g. level-5 Cohesion: 'Text organization consistently well controlled using a variety of effective linguistic features such as reference and transitional words and phrases...'). The rubric's dimensions map 1:1 onto the CSV score columns.
FORMAT: CSV — ELLIPSE_Final_github_train.csv header is text_id_kaggle, full_text, gender, grade, race_ethnicity, ..., prompt, Overall, Cohesion, Syntax, Vocabulary, Phraseology, Grammar, Conventions, set.
LICENSE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (NonCommercial + ShareAlike). Usable as dev/test fixtures; a blocker for redistribution inside a commercial product without separate permission.
ACCESS BARRIERS: mild — the test split and raw per-rater-score files are password-protected zips, with the passwords PUBLISHED IN THE README ('ellipse_test', 'ellipse_raw_data'). No DUA, no request form.
CAVEATS: it is a single corpus-wide L2-PROFICIENCY rubric, not per-assignment rubrics, and it scores English language proficiency rather than content mastery. Writers are grades 8-12, not higher-ed.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 2 TOP PICK — ASAG2024 (HuggingFace: Meyerger/ASAG2024) already merges SEVEN of the individually-requested short-answer grading datasets — SciEntsBank, Beetle II, Mohler & Mihalcea, SAF, Stita, CU-NLP, DigiKlausur — into one corpus with human grades on a unified scale.
findings.vote: 3-0 on composition (2 unanimous claims); the HF file-level specifics were separately refuted 1-2
findings.evidence:
NAME: ASAG2024: A Combined Benchmark for Short Answer Grading (Meyer, Breuer, Fürst — ZHAW), peer-reviewed at SIGCSE-Virtual 2024, ACM DOI 10.1145/3649409.3691083.
COMPOSITION (confirmed 3-0 against the PDF): STITA (Statistics, 333 items, 0-1), SAF English (CS, 2,463, 0-1), Mohler (Data Structures, 630, 0-5), SciEntsBank (science, 10,804, 4 categories), CU-NLP (NLP, 171, 0-100), Beetle II (Physics, ~3,941, 4 categories), DigiKlausur (ML, 646, 0-2). Subject coverage is science/CS/stats/physics — genuinely STEM.
HUMAN SCORES: YES — every row carries a human grade, normalized to a common scale. Row schema: question, provided_answer, reference_answer, grade, normalized_grade (0-1), data_source, weight.
RUBRICS: NO — rows carry REFERENCE ANSWERS, not rubrics. If Grader needs rubric-conditioned short-answer grading fixtures, reference answers are the substitute.
FORMAT / SIZE: HuggingFace dataset Meyerger/ASAG2024, reported ~56,646 rows (45.2k train / 5.7k val / 5.75k test), Parquet.
ACCESS BARRIERS: no gating/DUA reported on the HF repo.
IMPORTANT LICENSE WARNING: ASAG2024 does NOT confer a single clean license. The HF card states each constituent dataset retains its ORIGINAL license, so a commercial Grader must clear all seven upstream licenses individually. 'Packages them in one place' does not mean 'clears the licensing in one place.'
IMPORTANT FIDELITY WARNING: ASAG2024 is a NORMALIZED REPACKAGING, not a byte-identical mirror. Grades are rescaled to 0-1; SciEntsBank/Beetle II are natively 4-way CATEGORICAL, so their labels are transformed. If you need the original SemEval-2013 Task 7 5-way/3-way/2-way labels or the unseen-answers / unseen-questions / unseen-domains test splits, go to the ORIGINAL SemEval release instead.
CONFIDENCE NOTE: the benchmark's composition and human-grade content are 3-0 confirmed from the primary paper. A separate claim asserting the exact HF row counts, file size (~7.15 MB), Parquet format and 'no access gating' was REFUTED 1-2 — treat the precise HF file-level specs as unverified and re-check them at download time.
RECOMMENDATION (Category 2): pull ASAG2024 from HuggingFace as the single fastest source of human-graded STEM short answers; go to the original SemEval-2013 Task 7 (SciEntsBank/Beetle) release if you need the native categorical labels or the domain-transfer splits.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 2 SECOND PICK — S-GRADES (LREC 2026) consolidates 14 AES+ASAG datasets behind one download interface, but WITHHOLDS ground-truth labels on all test splits, so its test data cannot serve as local ground truth.
findings.evidence:
NAME: S-GRADES — Studying Generalization of Student Response Assessments in Diverse Evaluative Settings (Tasfia Seuti, Sagnik Ray Choudhury, UNT), arXiv 2603.10233, submitted 2026-03-10, accepted to LREC 2026. Paper CC BY 4.0. Platform https://sgrades.eng.unt.edu returns HTTP 200; code at https://github.com/nlpatunt/sgrades returns HTTP 200 (FastAPI, public).
CONTENTS: 14 datasets, >37K graded student responses, standardized train/val/test splits.
  AES (6): ASAP-AES (per-set ranges; 1,298 test), ASAP++ (0-6; 1,069), ASAP2.0 (0-6; 4,946), PERSUADE 2 (1-6; 2,600), IELTS Writing General (1-9; 144), IELTS Writing Task 2 (1-9; 491).
  ASAG (8): ASAP-SAS (0-3; 3,409), ReGrading 2JC (0-8; 198, NOT public), CSEE (0-16; 2,654), Mohler (0-5; 455, NOT public), Beetle (2-way/3-way; 1,258), SciEntsBank (2-way/3-way; 5,835), Rice_Chem (chemistry; per-question test splits of 60-66 for Q1-Q4), OS_Dataset (CS; NOT public; per-question splits, range 0-27).
SCHEMA: every dataset standardized to three core columns — Unique Identifier, Response Text, Ground Truth Score — with prompt texts, RUBRIC DESCRIPTIONS, essay_set identifiers and reference materials retained as SUPPLEMENTARY COLUMNS where the source provided them. (Heavyweight assets like source essays and images are linked by stable URL, not inlined.)
THE CRITICAL LIMITATION: train/val splits ship WITH labels; test splits ship WITHOUT them ('Test files keep metadata and identifiers but have ground-truth scores removed'). Evaluation is blind leaderboard submission — predictions are matched to privately-held ground truth server-side. So for local ground-truth testing in Grader, only train/val are usable from S-GRADES; for test-item ground truth you must go back to the original corpora (ASAP-AES, ASAP++, Mohler, Beetle/SciEntsBank are independently downloadable with labels).
LICENSE: the PAPER is CC BY 4.0; the DATA is not uniformly licensed. The paper says that for datasets not publicly hosted, 'we obtained creator permission for research use and sharing' — i.e. redistribution is RESEARCH-SCOPED, and each constituent carries its own upstream terms. Do not read 'downloadable' as 'commercially licensed.'
VALUE FOR GRADER: even if you never download it, S-GRADES Table 1 is the best single map of what graded-response data exists and which items are public vs not. It also confirms the existence of IELTS Writing score datasets and chemistry (Rice_Chem) / CS (OS_Dataset) graded corpora, though OS_Dataset, Mohler-as-hosted and ReGrading 2JC are flagged NOT public.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 2 / CS CODE GRADING — Menagerie is a genuinely public, MIT-licensed dataset of 667 CS1 Java assignment submissions of which ~272 carry human grades across four dimensions.
findings.evidence:
NAME: Menagerie: A Dataset of Graded Programming Assignments (SIGCSE TS 2025, ACM doi 10.1145/3641555.3705129; King's College London; OSF mirror osf.io/q8jbt).
SIZE: 667 total submissions of a second-semester CS1 Java predator/prey simulator (extends the classic foxes-and-rabbits template; groups of 2-3; OOP), collected over four academic years 2018/19-2021/22.
HUMAN SCORES: YES for a subset — 272 (README prose) / 273 (README file description) submissions were graded POST HOC by human graders as part of a study into human grader consistency (companion paper: 'How Consistent Are Humans When Grading Programming Assignments?', ACM TOCE, doi 10.1145/3759256). So ~60% of submissions (395 of 667) are UNGRADED; the usable graded set is ~272.
PATHS (verified to exist): data/anonymised_assignments/ (source code, organised by academic year) and data/grades.csv (grades + feedback for 273 assignments). Also present: data/template/, data/batches/, docstring_code_grades.csv, pre_study_survey.csv.
LICENSE: MIT — the most permissive license of anything in this report; commercially usable.
RUBRIC: NO formal levelled rubric matrix. Grades are PER-DIMENSION LETTER GRADES (correctness, elegance/design, readability, documentation) rather than a single numeric score; the only rubric-adjacent artifact is the assignment spec in data/template/.
ACCESS BARRIERS: none — public GitHub repo.
RECOMMENDATION: this is the one verified CS code-grading corpus with real human grades. Use it for the code-submission grading path; combine with ASAG2024's CS/NLP subsets (SAF, CU-NLP, DigiKlausur) for short-answer CS.

findings.claim: CATEGORY 3 (RUBRICS) — AAC&U's 16 VALUE rubrics are free to download as an OER bundle, but are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and AAC&U explicitly names 'Assessment software or digital products' as a commercial use requiring PRIOR WRITTEN PERMISSION. This directly gates shipping them as built-in templates in a commercial Grader.
findings.evidence:
WHAT: 16 VALUE rubrics (a 17th, 'Quantitative Literacy 2.0', now also appears), grouped as: Creative Thinking, Critical Thinking, Inquiry and Analysis, Problem Solving; Oral Communication, Reading, Written Communication; Information Literacy, Integrative Learning, Quantitative Literacy; Civic Engagement, Ethical Reasoning, Global Learning, Intercultural Knowledge and Competence; Foundations and Skills for Lifelong Learning, Teamwork. A 'Download All 16 VALUE Rubrics' bundle exists; no fee. These are genuine higher-ed rubrics (unlike the K-12 essay corpora above), which makes them the best domain fit for Grader's target user.
ACCESS: free; the download link routes through AAC&U's commerce/checkout flow, so expect a possible $0 email/account step.
LICENSE (the load-bearing finding): CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Note the license text is NOT on /value/rubrics (which only says 'freely available for educators to adapt and use') — it is on https://www.aacu.org/value/how-to-cite, which states: 'VALUE rubrics and ADD tools use the Creative Commons Attribution–NonCommercial–ShareAlike 4.0 International License'; 'The materials may not be used for commercial purposes that generate monetary or commercial advantage without prior permission'; and 'Requests to reproduce VALUE resources for commercial purposes must be submitted in writing to AAC&U' — with commercial uses ENUMERATED as: course packets sold to students; books or publications; commercial databases; and 'Assessment software or digital products.' The VALUE FAQ corroborates: 'VALUE rubrics can also be used in commercial databases, software, or assessment products with prior permission from AAC&U.'
PRACTICAL UPSHOT FOR GRADER: (a) VALUE rubrics are SAFE to use now as dev/test sample data and for non-commercial distribution (with attribution + ShareAlike). (b) If Grader is sold or monetized, bundling VALUE rubrics as built-in templates lands squarely in the enumerated 'assessment software or digital products' bucket and requires prior written permission — request path exists: value@aacu.org. It is permission-GATED, not prohibited; AAC&U does grant it, but approved commercial uses must reproduce the rubrics 'in their entirety and without modification' plus a permission statement. (c) ShareAlike binds only on DISTRIBUTION of an adaptation — purely internal adaptation triggers no obligation.
RECOMMENDATION (Category 3): use VALUE rubrics as the canonical higher-ed rubric fixtures during development, and email value@aacu.org early if the product will be commercial. For rubric+work+score TRIPLES (which VALUE does not provide), the only verified options are PERSUADE 2.0 (3 rubric PDFs) and ELLIPSE (ELL_Rubrics.docx) — no public university/Canvas Commons rubric library survived verification in this pass.

Treat those two arXiv IDs as unverified and likely hallucinated until confirmed.
  (5) DOCUMENT-PARSING TEST CORPORA — DocLayNet, OmniDocBench, PubLayNet. Nothing verified. result.caveats:
LICENSE IS THE DOMINANT CONSTRAINT, AND IT SPLITS CLEANLY. Only TWO verified resources are commercially usable: ASAP 2.0 (CC BY 4.0) and Menagerie (MIT). Everything else with real rubrics or analytic scores — PERSUADE 2.0, ELLIPSE, AAC&U VALUE — is NonCommercial (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and can be used for internal dev/testing but NOT bundled into a commercially shipped Grader without separate written permission. ASAG2024 and S-GRADES confer NO unified license at all: each constituent dataset retains its own upstream terms, so 'one download' does not mean 'one license.' If Grader is commercial, the safe bundle is ASAP 2.0 + Menagerie; everything else is dev-only until permissions are obtained.

DOMAIN MISMATCH. Every verified AES corpus (ASAP 2.0 grades 6-10, PERSUADE 2.0 grades 6-12, ELLIPSE grades 8-12) is K-12, not higher-ed. Grader targets higher-ed instructors. The scoring rubrics are holistic/SAT-style or L2-proficiency-style, not discipline-specific course rubrics. The AAC&U VALUE rubrics are the ONLY verified higher-ed-native artifact, and they come with no student work attached. There is currently NO verified corpus of higher-ed student work + course rubric + instructor grade.

DOUBLE-COUNTING. ASAP 2.0 and PERSUADE 2.0 share ~12,871 essays. Treating them as independent corpora inflates your effective sample by roughly half of ASAP 2.0.

TWO ARXIV IDS IN THE ORIGINAL QUESTION ARE SUSPECT. 2606.12422 and 2606.11477 (rubric-conditioned grading; handwritten exam answer recognition) were flagged as possibly non-existent by a verifier. 2510.17389 was never checked. 2603.10233 (S-GRADES) and 2409.18596 (ASAG2024) DID independently resolve and are real.

UNVERIFIED SECONDARY DETAILS. The Kaggle competition '3 files / 36.2 MB' figure could not be confirmed while logged out. The exact HuggingFace file specs for Meyerger/ASAG2024 (row counts, 7.15 MB, Parquet, no gating) were REFUTED 1-2 and should be re-checked at download time — the benchmark's composition and human grades are solid, the file-level metadata is not. S-GRADES' per-dataset schema conformance is self-reported in an unrefereed preprint; nobody downloaded all 14 to confirm.

TIME-SENSITIVITY. The Learning Agency Lab states it 'is no longer active,' so the ASAP 2.0 landing page may rot (the Kaggle mirror was last updated 2025-12-05 and is live). S-GRADES is a ~4-month-old preprint with a live but young platform. Password-protected splits use passwords published in READMEs (asap2_test, persuade_test, ellipse_test, ellipse_raw_data) — these could change.

FOUR OF SEVEN CATEGORIES WERE NOT ANSWERED. Handwriting, document-parsing, citation-verification, and Canvas testing produced no surviving claims. This is a coverage gap in the research, not evidence that no options exist.
openQuestions: Does ANY public dataset pair HIGHER-ED student work with the instructor's actual course rubric and the actual grade awarded? Every verified corpus is K-12, and the only higher-ed rubrics found (AAC&U VALUE) ship with no student work. If the answer is no, Grader may need to generate its own gold set with a partner instructor — which is a product/timeline decision, not a research one.

Will AAC&U grant permission to embed the 16 VALUE rubrics in a commercial AI grading product, and on what terms (fee, attribution, 'entirety and without modification' constraint)? This is answerable today by emailing value@aacu.org and materially affects whether Grader can ship rubric templates out of the box.

Are arXiv 2606.12422, 2606.11477 and 2510.17389 real papers? Two were flagged as likely hallucinated IDs. If the handwritten-exam-answer-recognition paper does not exist, category 4 has no starting point and needs to be rebuilt from IAM/CROHME/CVL/RIMES first principles.

Is there any public corpus of real-vs-fabricated citations, or of student papers with bibliographies? Category 6 is the one most likely to have NO good public option, and Grader's citation-verification feature cannot be validated without either such a corpus or a synthetic fixture set built from Crossref/OpenAlex plus deliberately corrupted DOIs.

refuted.claim: The corpus is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — NonCommercial — so it can be used for development/testing/benchmarking but NOT redistributed or used in a commercial product's shipped assets without violating terms.

The dataset is publicly downloadable from HuggingFace as Meyerger/ASAG2024 with no access gating: 56,646 rows (train 45.2k / validation 5.7k / test 5.75k), ~7.15 MB, Parquet format, containing question text, student answer, reference answer, and HUMAN grade (0-100 plus a normalized 0-1 field) — i.e. it has human scores and reference answers, but reference answers rather than explicit rubrics.
